# Education and Outreach

Outreach is a central part of the lab’s work. We spend time leading field tours, developing classroom materials, meeting with land managers, and helping journalists and filmmakers explain prairie research. These exchanges also shape our research.

For instance, the Konza Environmental Education Program (KEEP), led by Jill Haukos and High School Teachers, has created a [high-school biology module](https://keep.konza.k-state.edu/education/Highschool_Storyline.html){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"} that currently reaches around 1,000 students per year. Students use the prairie as a lens to learn core biological principles and their home ecoregion at the same time. Our lab has contributed filmed interviews, maps, and graphs to a six-week classroom module.

## Teaching

Our teaching connects ecological concepts with questions students can investigate using field observations, experiments, and data. At Konza Prairie, students can examine how plant communities respond to fire, grazing, and climate, drawing on their own observations and long-term records. Across courses, we emphasize developing questions, comparing explanations, and interpreting evidence.

-   Ecology (BIOL 529): every fall.
-   Community Ecology (BIOL 857): fall of even-numbered years.
-   Environmental Resilience (BIOL 858): fall of odd-numbered years.

Students interested in an independent study or a related research project are welcome to get in touch.
